title: Cross-Workload Evaluation Safety and Quantization Verification Protocol
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

This document defines a lightweight, prescriptive protocol to validate that quantized model artifacts and evaluation harness changes are safe to promote across multiple workload profiles. It is intended for applied ML engineers, model onboarding owners, and SREs involved in model rollout and regression triage.

Goals

- Provide a deterministic evaluation sequence to catch accuracy regressions introduced by quantization or inference kernel changes.
- Standardize cross-workload scorecards and pass/fail criteria so rollouts are consistent across teams.
- Define immediate triage and rollback actions for failures with clear owners and timelines.

Scope

- Applies to: floating-point -> quantized conversions (INT8/FP16/4-bit), new kernel/backing runtime variants, and inference-serving shims that change KV-cache behavior.
- Not in scope: upstream model training changes (handled by model-training certification) and customer-specific prompt re-labeling.

Definitions

- Workload profile: a representative request distribution (e.g., short-chat, long-context-summarization, embeddings-batch).
- Golden reference: a certified model artifact previously validated for the same workload profile.
- Delta-test: a deterministic run comparing a candidate artifact against the golden reference using the eval harness.

Owners and Roles

- Model Owner: leads artifact conversion and initial validation.
- Eval Owner: configures and runs the eval harness, computes metrics and stores artifacts in the eval bucket.
- Oncall SRE: responsible for rollout monitoring, alerting, and emergency rollback under the shift-left plan.
- Product Safety Reviewer: performs subjective checks on prompt-sensitive regressions for high-risk workloads.

Preconditions

1) Candidate artifact uploaded to artifact storage with a unique tag and provenance metadata. Required metadata keys: model_name, commit_sha, quant_profile, build_time, base_model_id.
2) Eval harness CI pipeline has access to workload profiles and the standard prompt set.
3) Monitoring dashboards and alerting rules referenced in this doc exist in the Redwood Console for the model route.

Evaluation Sequence (delta-test)

1. Select the workload matrix: at minimum, run the candidate against three canonical profiles: short-chat (<=128 tokens), long-context (>=2048 tokens), and batch-embeddings (1k requests, batch=64).
2. Generate deterministic prompt seeds: use the approved seed list for the workload profile (stored at /eval/prompt-sets/crossworkload-seeds.csv).
3. Run the eval harness in headless mode with identical runtime flags to production. Command example:

```bash
# Example: run delta-test for short-chat profile
redwood-eval-run --profile short-chat --candidate s3://artifacts/candidate:tag --golden s3://artifacts/golden:stable --out results/candidate_vs_golden_short-chat.json --deterministic --no-random-seed-offset
```

4. Compute the following metrics for each profile: exact-match (where applicable), ROUGE-L, BLEU (for templated tasks), embedding-similarity (cosine), latency P50/P95, and token-efficiency (tokens consumed per useful-output token).

Pass/Fail Criteria

- Numerical thresholds (per-profile):
  - Short-chat: embedding-similarity >= 0.985 AND latency P95 <= baseline_P95 * 1.15 AND no prompt-set hallucination events > 0.5%
  - Long-context: ROUGE-L delta >= -1.5 points relative to golden AND coherence regressions (per human-annotated set) <= 2%
  - Batch-embeddings: average cosine similarity >= 0.99 AND throughput >= baseline_throughput * 0.9
- If any metric crosses a critical alert boundary (embedding-similarity drop > 0.02 or latency P95 > baseline * 1.5), automatically mark as FAIL and escalate.

Quality Guardrails and Safety Checks

- Prompt-sensitive regression list: run a curated list of 200 high-value, adversarial prompts. Any regression flagged by the Product Safety Reviewer requires manual review even if numeric metrics pass.
- Token-truncation safety: ensure the candidate preserves top-K token continuity for KV-cache-sensitive tasks. Run the KV continuity probe with K=8 across long-contexts.
- Behavioral delta detection: run an automatic style-change classifier to detect shifts in politeness, bias markers, or content policy violations. Any detected content-policy change must be escalated to Security & Compliance.

Regression Triage Procedure (if FAIL)

1. Triage owner (Model Owner) must acknowledge within 2 business hours and open a regression ticket with the delta-test artifacts and the primary failing metric.
2. Run targeted A/B tests: run candidate vs golden on a narrowed subset of prompts (the top 20 failing seeds) with human raters (3 raters, majority vote) within 48 hours.
3. If human raters confirm failure: revert rollout, mark artifact as blocked, notify customers if impacted per incident policy.

Fast Recovery Playbook (criticality-based)

- Critical (customer-facing degradation or SLA breach): immediate rollout pause + rollback within 30 minutes. Oncall SRE to trigger rollback playbook.
- High (significant drop in model quality but no SLA breach): pause automated promotions and open hotfix ticket. Model Owner to produce a follow-up candidate within 5 business days.
- Medium/Low: monitor with enhanced sampling for 7 days and run an expanded eval set.

Rollout Gating and Automation

- Gates enforced in CI: delta-test must pass for all three canonical profiles and the prompt-sensitive regression list.
- Canary rollout: 1% traffic for 24 hours with increased logging and golden-traffic shadowing. Canary metrics must show no anomalies (P95, embedding-similarity, error-rate).
- Automated promotion: after 72 hours with stable metrics, increase to 10% for 48 hours, then full promotion if stable. Any anomaly triggers rollback.

Monitoring and Alerting

- Dashboards to include per-profile embedding-similarity heatmaps, prompt-set regression counters, latency percentiles, and token-efficiency trends.
- Alerts:
  - Critical alert: embedding-similarity drop > 0.02 OR external SLA latency breach -> Pager duty page.
  - Warning alert: embedding-similarity drop in [0.01,0.02] OR P95 latency increase 1.15x -> Slack channel + ticket.

Example Config Snippet (eval pipeline YAML)

```yaml
pipeline: delta-test
profiles:
  - short-chat
  - long-context
  - batch-embeddings
candidate: s3://artifacts/candidate:{{BUILD_TAG}}
golden: s3://artifacts/golden:stable
metrics:
  - embedding_similarity
  - rouge_l
  - latency_p95
pass_criteria:
  short-chat:
    embedding_similarity: 0.985
    latency_p95_ratio: 1.15
  long-context:
    rouge_l_delta: -1.5
  batch-embeddings:
    cosine: 0.99
```

Investigation checklist (post-failure)

- Reproduce with identical runtime flags and hardware (GPU type, sequence-length cap, kernel flags).
- Compare tokenization outputs for edge-cases and byte-level diffs.
- Re-run with progressive de-quantization (FP16 -> INT8) to isolate when behavior diverged.
- If regression only appears under production-serving runtime, run local microbench with the same runtime binary and trace at attention-kernel level.

Record-keeping and Artifact Storage

- Store all delta-test artifacts under s3://eval-results/{model_name}/{candidate_tag}/ with a manifest.json that includes metric summaries and provenance.
- Attach the manifest to the regression ticket and link it in the model onboarding checklist.

Appendix: Quick triage CLI snippets

```bash
# summarize metrics
redwood-eval-summary --input results/candidate_vs_golden_short-chat.json --out results/summary_short-chat.txt

# run a targeted AB subset with 20 seeds and 3 human raters
redwood-eval-run --profile short-chat --seeds seeds/top20_short_chat.txt --human-raters 3 --candidate s3://artifacts/candidate:tag --golden s3://artifacts/golden:stable --out results/ab_top20.json
```
